title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 131 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 613–618 (Night 131, continuing directly from nights-130), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 131 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. The envoys come home with the lady Dunyā’s refusal, and King Sulaymān Shāh is talked out of making war, for she has sworn to kill any husband forced on her and then herself. Tāj al-Mulūk resolves to reach her in disguise as a merchant; with the old vizier and ʿAzīz as guide he travels four months, weeping and reciting verse, until the White Castle comes into view. In the city the vizier passes himself off as an old merchant travelling with his two sons, and the headman of the cloth market, much taken with the two young men, gives them the finest shop in the covered market. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu wa-al-thalāthūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the first and the thirty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and thirty-first night,
sentences.n: The print spells thalāthūn without its long alif (ثلثون), its usual spelling; the dagger alif marks the long vowel.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ قَالَ لِلْوَزِيرِ وَعَزِيزٍ سَلِّمَا عَلَى الْمَلِكِ وَإِنَّكُمَا تُخْبِرَانِ الْمَلِكَ بِمَا سَمِعْتُمَاهُ بِأَنَّ ابْنَتِى لَاتُحِبُّ الزَّوَاجَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malika shahramāna qāla li-al-wazīri wa-ʿazīzin sallimā ʿalā al-maliki wa-innakumā tukhbirāni al-malika bi-mā samiʿtumāhu bi-anna ibnatī lā tuḥibbu al-zawāja
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that King Shahramān said to the vizier and ʿAzīz: Give-greeting (you two) to the king, and (truly) you two shall tell the king of what you have heard, that my daughter does-not love the marriage.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that King Shahramān said to the vizier and to ʿAzīz, “Greet your king for me, and tell him what you have heard: that my daughter does not wish to marry.”
sentences.n: Shahramān is the king of the Camphor Islands, Dunyā’s father, sending the envoys home. wa-innakumā tukhbirāni, “and you two shall tell”: the imperfect after inna serves as a polite command. akhbara bi-, “to inform of”: bi- names what is told, here twice over (bi-mā … bi-anna). The print sets lā tuḥibbu as one word (لاتحب), and writes ibnatī with a final ى; kept.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ فَائِدَةٍ وَمَازَالُوا مُسَافِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلُوا عَلَى الْمَلِكِ وَأَخْبَرُوهُ بِمَاجَرَي
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿū min ghayri fāʾidatin wa-mā zālū musāfirīna ilā an dakhalū ʿalā al-maliki wa-akhbarūhu bi-mā jarā
sentences.l: So they returned without profit, and they did not cease travelling until they went-in to the king and informed him of what had happened.
sentences.i: So they went back with nothing gained, and travelled on until they came before their king and told him what had happened.
sentences.n: The print runs mā zālū and bi-mā jarā together (ومازالوا, بماجري) and writes jarā with a final ي; kept.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمَرَ النُّقَبَاءَ أَنْ يُنَادُوا عَلَى الْعَسَاكِرِ بِالسَّفَرِ مِنْ أَجْلِ الْحَرْبِ وَالْجِهَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika amara al-nuqabāʾa an yunādū ʿalā al-ʿasākiri bi-al-safari min ajli al-ḥarbi wa-al-jihādi
sentences.l: And at that he ordered the officers that they call-out to the troops with the setting-out, for the sake of the war and the holy-war.
sentences.i: At that the king ordered his officers to call the troops to march, for war and holy war.
sentences.n: nādā ʿalā … bi-, “to cry out to … for”: bi- names what is proclaimed. nuqabāʾ (sing. naqīb) are officers who carry orders to the troops. al-ḥarb wa-al-jihād, “war and holy war”, is the tale’s stock pairing.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ لَاتَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّ الْمَلِكَ لَا ذَنْبَ لَهُ وَإِنَّ ابْنَتَهُ حِينَ عَلِمَتْ بِذَلِكَ أَرْسَلَتْ تَقُولُ إِنْ غَصَبَنِى أَبِي عَلَى الزَّوَاجِ أَقْتُلْ مَنْ أَتَزَوَّجُ بِهِ وَأَقْتُلْ نَفْسِي بَعْدَهُ وَإِنَّمَا الِامْتِنَاعُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru ayyuhā al-maliku lā tafʿal dhālika fa-inna al-malika lā dhanba lahu wa-inna ibnatahu ḥīna ʿalimat bi-dhālika arsalat taqūlu in ghaṣabanī abī ʿalā al-zawāji aqtul man atazawwaju bihi wa-aqtul nafsī baʿdahu wa-innamā al-imtināʿu minhā
sentences.l: And the vizier said to him: O king, do-not do that, for the king, no fault (is) to him; and his daughter, when she knew of that, sent saying: If my father forces me upon the marriage, I kill whom I marry (with), and I kill myself after him. And only the refusal (is) from her.
sentences.i: But the vizier said to him, “O king, do not do it. Her father is not to blame. When his daughter heard of it, she sent word: ‘If my father forces me to marry, I will kill the man I marry, and kill myself after him.’ The refusal is hers alone.”
sentences.n: ʿalima bi-, “to learn of”: the verb takes bi- for what is learned. ghaṣaba ʿalā, “to force into”. tazawwaja bi-, “to marry”: the verb often takes bi- for the spouse. innamā, “only”: the refusal comes from her and no one else. The print sets lā tafʿal as one word (لاتفعل) and writes ghaṣabanī with a final ى; kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ كَلَامَ الْوَزِيرِ خَافَ عَلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَقَالَ إِنْ أَنَا حَارَبْتُ أَبَاهَا وَظَفِرْتُ بِابْنَتِهِ فَهِيَ تَقْتُلُ نَفْسَهَا فَلَا يُفِيدُنِي شَئٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku kalāma al-wazīri khāfa ʿalā tāji al-mulūki wa-qāla in anā ḥārabtu abāhā wa-ẓafirtu bi-ibnatihi fa-hiya taqtulu nafsahā fa-lā yufīdunī shayʾun
sentences.l: And when the king heard the speech of the vizier, he feared for Tāj al-Mulūk, and said: If I, I fight her father and win (with) his daughter, then she kills herself, so nothing profits me.
sentences.i: When the king heard the vizier’s words he feared for Tāj al-Mulūk, and said, “If I make war on her father and win his daughter, she will kill herself, and I shall have gained nothing.”
sentences.n: in anā ḥārabtu, “if I, I make war”: the pronoun before the verb stresses the speaker. ẓafira bi-, “to win, lay hold of”: the verb takes bi- for the prize. The print spells shayʾ as شئ, as it often does.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَعْلَمَ ابْنَهُ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika aʿlama ibnahu tāja al-mulūki bi-dhālika
sentences.l: Then (truly) the king informed his son Tāj al-Mulūk of that.
sentences.i: Then the king told his son Tāj al-Mulūk of this.
sentences.n: aʿlama … bi-, “to inform … of”: bi- names what is made known.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبِي أَنَا لَا أُطِيقُ الصَّبْرَ عَنْهَا فَأَنَا أَرُوحُ إِلَيْهَا وَأَتَحَايَلُ فِي اتِّصَالِي بِهَا وَلَوْ أَمُوتُ وَلَا أَفْعَلُ غَيْرَ هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalima dhālika qāla li-abīhi yā abī anā lā uṭīqu al-ṣabra ʿanhā fa-anā arūḥu ilayhā wa-ataḥāyalu fī ittiṣālī bihā wa-law amūtu wa-lā afʿalu ghayra hādhā
sentences.l: And when he knew that, he said to his father: O my father, I, I cannot-bear the patience (away) from her; so I, I go to her and contrive in my joining with her, even if I die; and I do not do other than this.
sentences.i: When he learned it, he said to his father, “Father, I cannot bear to be without her. I will go to her myself and find some trick to reach her, even if it kills me; I will do nothing else.”
sentences.n: rāḥa, “to go”, is the spoken verb for dhahaba. taḥāyala fī, “to use cunning in”. ittiṣāl bi-, “joining with, union with”: bi- names the one joined. wa-law amūtu, “even if I die”, with the imperfect where Classical would use the perfect.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُوهُ وَكَيْفَ تَرُوحُ إِلَيْهَا فَقَالَ أَرُوحُ فِي صِفَةِ تَاجِرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu abūhu wa-kayfa tarūḥu ilayhā fa-qāla arūḥu fī ṣifati tājirin
sentences.l: And his father said to him: And how do you go to her? And he said: I go in the description of a merchant.
sentences.i: His father said, “And how will you go to her?” He said, “I will go in the guise of a merchant.”
sentences.n: fī ṣifat, “in the description of”, i.e. disguised as.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنْ كَانَ وَلَا بُدَّ فَخُذْ مَعَكَ الْوَزِيرَ وَعَزِيزًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku in kāna wa-lā budda fa-khudh maʿaka al-wazīra wa-ʿazīzan
sentences.l: And the king said: If it is, and no escape, then take with you the vizier and ʿAzīz.
sentences.i: The king said, “If it must be, then take the vizier and ʿAzīz with you.”
sentences.n: in kāna wa-lā budda, “if it is, and there is no help for it”: a fixed phrase, “if you must”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَخْرَجَ لَهُ شَيْأً مِنْ خَزَائِنِهِ وَهَيَّأَ لَهُ مَتْجَرًا بِمِائَةِ أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَاتَّفَقَا مَعَهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu akhraja lahu shayʾan min khazāʾinihi wa-hayyaʾa lahu matjaran bi-miʾati alfi dīnārin wa-ittafaqā maʿahu ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: Then (truly) he brought out for him a thing from his treasuries, and prepared for him a merchandise with (the worth of) a hundred thousand dinars; and the two agreed with him on that.
sentences.i: Then the king brought out treasure for him from his storehouses and made ready a stock of goods worth a hundred thousand dinars, and the two agreed with the prince on the plan.
sentences.n: shayʾan, “something”, here “some (treasure)”: the print spells it شيأ, with the hamza on an alif, and points its tanwīn itself. matjar, “stock-in-trade”; bi- gives its price. ittafaqā, “the two agreed”: the vizier and ʿAzīz.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاءَ اللَّيْلُ ذَهَبَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَعَزِيزٌ إِلَى مَنْزِلِ عَزِيزٍ وَبَاتَا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ هُنَاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾa al-laylu dhahaba tāju al-mulūki wa-ʿazīzun ilā manzili ʿazīzin wa-bātā tilka al-laylata hunāka
sentences.l: And when the night came, Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz went to the dwelling of ʿAzīz, and the two passed-the-night that night there.
sentences.i: When night came, Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz went to ʿAzīz’s house and spent the night there.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ مَسْلُوبَ الْفُؤَادِ وَلَمْ يَطِبْ لَهُ أَكْلٌ وَلَارُقَادٌ بَلْ هَجَمَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِكْرُ وَهَزَّهُ الشَّوْقُ إِلَى مَحْبُوبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra tāju al-mulūki maslūba al-fuʾādi wa-lam yaṭib lahu aklun wa-lā ruqādun bal hajama ʿalayhi al-fikru wa-hazzahu al-shawqu ilā maḥbūbatihi
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk became robbed of the heart, and there was not pleasant to him eating nor sleeping; rather the thought rushed upon him, and the longing for his beloved shook him.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk was robbed of his heart; neither food nor sleep was sweet to him, but brooding fell upon him, and longing for his beloved shook him.
sentences.n: The prose rhymes on fuʾād and ruqād. The print sets wa-lā ruqād as one word (ولارقاد); kept.

sentences.t: فَتَوَسَّلَ بِالْخَلَّاقِ أَنْ يَمُنَّ عَلَيْهِ بِالتَّلَاقِ وَبَكَى وَأَنَّ وَاشْتَكَى وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-tawassala bi-al-khallāqi an yamunna ʿalayhi bi-al-talāqi wa-bakā wa-anna wa-ishtakā wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And he implored (by) the Creator that He grant him (with) the meeting, and he wept and moaned and complained, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: He besought the Creator to grant him the joy of meeting her, and he wept and moaned and lamented, and recited:
sentences.n: tawassala bi-, “to plead by, to call on”: bi- names the one appealed to. manna ʿalā … bi-, “to bestow … on”, with bi- for the gift. al-talāq, “the meeting (of lovers)”, rhymes with al-khallāq. anna, “he moaned”, from anīn, “moaning”.

sentences.t:
تَرَى هَلْ لَنَا بَعْدَ الْبِعَادِ وُصُوْلُ * فَاَشْكُوْ الَيْكُمْ صَبْوَتِي وَاَقُوْلُ
تَذَكَّرْتُكُمْ وَاللَّيْلُ فِي غَفَلَاتِهِ * وَاَسْهَرْتُمُوْنِي وَالْاَنَامُ غَفُوْلُ
sentences.tr:
tarā hal lanā baʿda al-biʿādi wuṣūlu * fa-ashkū ilaykum ṣabwatī wa-aqūlu
tadhakkartukum wa-al-laylu fī ghafalātihi * wa-ashartumūnī wa-al-anāmu ghafūlu
sentences.l:
Do you see (whether) there is to us, after the distance, an arrival (at union), * so I complain to you of my yearning and I say:
I remembered you, and the night (was) in its heedlessnesses, * and you made-me-wakeful, and the creatures (are) heedless.
sentences.i:
Shall we, I wonder, after this distance ever be united, * so that I may tell you my longing and say:
“I remembered you while the night lay heedless, * and you kept me waking while all creation slept.”
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. tarā, “do you see?”, opens a wondering question: “I wonder”. The print writes ilaykum without its hamza (الَيْكُمْ). The final -u of wuṣūlu and aqūlu is the rhyme vowel. ashara, “to keep awake”; al-anām, “mankind, all creatures”; ghafūl, “heedless”, here “asleep”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ بَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَبَكَى مَعَهُ عَزِيزٌ وَتَذَكَّرَ ابْنَةَ عَمِّهِ وَلَا زَالَا كَذَلِكَ يَبْكِيَانِ إِلَى أَنْ أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi bakā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-bakā maʿahu ʿazīzun wa-tadhakkara ibnata ʿammihi wa-lā zālā ka-dhālika yabkiyāni ilā an aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu
sentences.l: And when he finished from his poetry, he wept a weeping severe, and ʿAzīz wept with him and remembered the daughter of his paternal-uncle; and the two did not cease thus, weeping, until the morning dawned.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses he wept bitterly, and ʿAzīz wept with him, remembering his cousin; and so the two went on weeping until morning came.
sentences.n: ibnat ʿammihi, “his father’s brother’s daughter”: ʿAzīza, the cousin ʿAzīz was to marry, who died of grief for him. wa-lā zālā, “and the two did not cease”, with lā where Classical has mā.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى وَالِدَتِهِ وَهُوَ لَابِسٌ أُهْبَةَ السَّفَرِ فَسَأَلَتْهُ عَنْ حَالِهِ فَأَعَادَ عَلَيْهَا الْخَبَرَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāma tāju al-mulūki wa-dakhala ʿalā wālidatihi wa-huwa lābisun uhbata al-safari fa-saʾalathu ʿan ḥālihi fa-aʿāda ʿalayhā al-khabara
sentences.l: Then Tāj al-Mulūk rose and went-in to his mother, and he (was) wearing the gear of the journey; and she asked him about his state, and he repeated to her the news.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk rose and went in to his mother, dressed for the journey. She asked him how things stood, and he told her the whole story.
sentences.n: uhbat al-safar, “the gear of travel”. aʿāda ʿalayhā al-khabar, “he repeated the story to her”, the tale’s way of saying he told her everything.

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَتْهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ ثُمَّ وَدَّعَتْهُ وَخَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا وَدَعَتْ لَهُ بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَالِاجْتِمَاعِ بِالْأَحْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭathu khamsīna alfa dīnārin thumma waddaʿathu wa-kharaja min ʿindihā wa-daʿat lahu bi-al-salāmati wa-al-ijtimāʿi bi-al-aḥbābi
sentences.l: And she gave him fifty thousand dinars; then she bade-him-farewell, and he went out from her presence, and she prayed for him with the safety and the meeting with the beloved-ones.
sentences.i: She gave him fifty thousand dinars and bade him farewell, and he left her, while she prayed that he would be kept safe and be united with those he loved.
sentences.n: daʿā lahu bi-, “to pray for him for”: bi- names what is asked for; ijtimāʿ bi-, “meeting with”. waddaʿathu, “she bade him farewell”, and daʿat lahu, “she prayed for him”, look alike but are different verbs.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عَلَى وَالِدِهِ وَاسْتَأْذَنَهُ أَنْ يَرْحَلَ فَأَذِنَ لَهُ وَأَعْطَاهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَأَمَرَأَنْ تُضْرَبَ لَهُ خَيْمَةٌ فِي خَارِجِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala ʿalā wālidihi wa-istaʾdhanahu an yarḥala fa-adhina lahu wa-aʿṭāhu khamsīna alfa dīnārin wa-amara an tuḍraba lahu khaymatun fī khāriji al-madīnati
sentences.l: Then he went-in to his father and asked his leave that he depart; and he permitted him, and gave him fifty thousand dinars, and ordered that a tent be pitched for him in (the) outside of the city.
sentences.i: Then he went in to his father and asked leave to set out. His father gave it, and gave him fifty thousand dinars, and ordered a tent to be pitched for him outside the city.
sentences.n: The print runs amara and an together (وامران); kept. ḍaraba khayma, “to pitch (literally strike) a tent”.

sentences.t: فَضُرِبَتْ لَهُ الْخَيْمَةُ فَأَقَامَ فِيهَا يَوْمَيْنِ وَسَافَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍuribat lahu al-khaymatu fa-aqāma fīhā yawmayni wa-sāfara
sentences.l: And the tent was pitched for him, and he stayed in it two days, and travelled.
sentences.i: The tent was pitched, and he stayed in it two days and then set out.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَأْنَسَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ بِعَزِيزٍ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي أَنَا مَا بَقِيتُ أُطِيقُ أَنْ أُفَارِقَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-istaʾnasa tāju al-mulūki bi-ʿazīzin wa-qāla lahu yā akhī anā mā baqītu uṭīqu an ufāriqaka
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk took-comfort with ʿAzīz, and said to him: O my brother, I, I no longer can-bear that I part from you.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk found comfort in ʿAzīz’s company and said to him, “Brother, I can no longer bear to be parted from you.”
sentences.n: The print has تأج, a misprint for تاج, corrected here. istaʾnasa bi-, “to find company and comfort in”: bi- names the companion. mā baqītu uṭīqu, “I no longer can bear”: baqiya with a negative and a following verb is the spoken “no longer”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَزِيزٌ وَأَنَا الْآخَرُ كَذَلِكَ وَأَنَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَمُوتَ تَحْتَ رِجْلَيْكَ وَلَكِنْ يَا أَخِي قَلْبِي اشْتَغَلَ بِوَالِدَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿazīzun wa-anā al-ākharu ka-dhālika wa-anā uḥibbu an amūta taḥta rijlayka wa-lākin yā akhī qalbī ishtaghala bi-wālidatī
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz said: And I, the other, (am) likewise, and I, I love that I die under your two feet; but, O my brother, my heart has become-occupied with my mother.
sentences.i: ʿAzīz said, “And so it is with me; I would gladly die at your feet. But, brother, my heart is troubled for my mother.”
sentences.n: wa-anā al-ākhar, “and I too”, literally “and I the other”, a spoken idiom. ishtaghala bi-, “to be preoccupied with”: bi- names the cause of worry.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ لَمَّا نَبْلُغُ الْمَرَامَ لَايَكُونُ إِلَّا خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu tāju al-mulūki lammā nablughu al-marāma lā yakūnu illā khayran
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said to him: When we reach the goal, there will not be except good.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said to him, “When we have reached our goal, all will be well.”
sentences.n: lammā, “when”, with the imperfect for a time to come, as in speech. The print sets lā yakūnu as one word (لايكون); kept.

sentences.t: وَسَافَرُوا وَكَانَ الْوَزِيرُ قَدْ أَوْصَى تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ بِالِاصْطِبَارِ وَصَارَ عَزِيزٌ يُسَامِرُهُ وَيُنْشِدُ لَهُ الْأَشْعَارَ وَيُحَدِّثُهُ بِالتَّوَارِيخِ وَالْأَخْبَارِ وَهُمْ يَجِدُّونَ فِى السَّيْرِ لَيْلًا وَ نَهَارًا مُدَّةَ شَهْرَيْنِ كَوَامِلَ
sentences.tr: wa-sāfarū wa-kāna al-wazīru qad awṣā tāja al-mulūki bi-al-iṣṭibāri wa-ṣāra ʿazīzun yusāmiruhu wa-yunshidu lahu al-ashʿāra wa-yuḥaddithuhu bi-al-tawārīkhi wa-al-akhbāri wa-hum yajiddūna fī al-sayri laylan wa-nahāran muddata shahrayni kawāmila
sentences.l: And they travelled; and the vizier had enjoined Tāj al-Mulūk with the patience; and ʿAzīz began to talk-by-night with him, and recite to him the poems, and tell him (of) the histories and the stories, and they (were) hastening in the going, night and day, a space of two months complete.
sentences.i: So they travelled. The vizier had urged Tāj al-Mulūk to be patient, and ʿAzīz kept him company in the evenings, reciting poems to him and telling him histories and tales, while they pressed on night and day for two whole months.
sentences.n: The prose rhymes on iṣṭibār, ashʿār and akhbār. awṣā … bi-, “to enjoin … to”: bi- names what is urged. ḥaddatha … bi-, “to tell … of”. sāmara, “to keep (someone) company in night-talk” (samar). jadda fī al-sayr, “to press on with the journey”. The print breaks the line between wa- and nahāran (ليلا و / نهارا); the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَطَالَتِ الطَّرِيقُ عَلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَزَادَتْ بِهِ النِّيرَانُ فَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭālati al-ṭarīqu ʿalā tāji al-mulūki wa-zādat bihi al-nīrānu fa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And the road grew-long upon Tāj al-Mulūk, and the fires increased in him; and he recited, saying:
sentences.i: The road grew long for Tāj al-Mulūk, and the fires within him burned higher, and he recited:
sentences.n: ṭarīq, “road”, is feminine here (ṭālat), as it may be. zādat bihi al-nīrān, “the fires increased in him”: bi- here means “in, within”.

sentences.t:
طَالَ الْمَسِيرُ وَزَادَ الْهَمُّ وَالْقَلَق * وَفِي الْفُؤَادِ هَوًى زَادَتْ بِهِ الْحُرَقِ
اَقْسَمْتُ يَا مُنْيَتِي يَامُنْتَهَى اَمَلِيْ * بِحَقِّ مَنْ خَلَقَ الْانْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقِ
لَقَدْ حَمَلْتُ غَرَامًا مِنْكِ يَاسُؤْلِيْ * لَمْ تَحْمِلْنَهُ جِبَالُ الشُّمِّ بِالْاَرَقِ
يَاسِتَّ دُنْيَايَ اِنَّ الْحُبَّ اَهْلَكَنِيْ * وَرَدَّنِي مَيِّتًا مَافِيَّ مِنْ رَمَقِ
لَوْلَا الرَّجَاءُ بِوَصْلٍ مِنْكَ يُطْمِعُنِيْ * مَاكَانَ شَخْصِي اَتَى فِى السَّيْرِ مُنْطَلِقِ
sentences.tr:
ṭāla al-masīru wa-zāda al-hammu wa-al-qalaq * wa-fī al-fuʾādi hawan zādat bihi al-ḥuraqi
aqsamtu yā munyatī yā muntahā amalī * bi-ḥaqqi man khalaqa al-insāna min ʿalaqi
laqad ḥamaltu gharāman minki yā suʾlī * lam taḥmilnahu jibālu al-shummi bi-al-araqi
yā sitta dunyāya inna al-ḥubba ahlakanī * wa-raddanī mayyitan mā fiyya min ramaqi
lawlā al-rajāʾu bi-waṣlin minka yuṭmiʿunī * mā kāna shakhṣī atā fī al-sayri munṭaliqi
sentences.l:
The journey has grown-long, and the care and the anxiety have increased, * and in the heart (is) a passion by which the burnings have increased.
I have sworn, O my wish, O utmost of my hope, * by the right of Him who created man from a clot,
truly I have carried a love-torment from you, O my request, * (such as) the lofty mountains would not carry, with the sleeplessness.
O Lady of my world, truly the love has destroyed me * and returned me dead, there is not in me of a last-breath.
Were it not for the hope of a union from you (that) makes me covet, * my person would not have come in the going, setting-off.
sentences.i:
The road is long, and care and unrest have grown, * and in my heart is a love that makes the burning grow.
I swear, my wish, the very end of all my hope, * by Him who made man from a clot of blood,
I bear such a passion for you, my one desire, * as the high mountains could not bear, with all this sleeplessness.
O Lady of my world, my love has ruined me, * and left me dead, without a breath of life.
Were it not for the hope of union with you that lures me on, * I would never have set out upon this road.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. yā sitta dunyāya, “O lady of my world”, plays on the beloved’s name, Sitt Dunyā, “Lady World”. man khalaqa al-insāna min ʿalaq, “Him who created man from a clot”, echoes the Qurʾān (96:2); bi-ḥaqqi, “by the right of”, is the formula of an oath. al-shumm, “the lofty”, plural of ashamm, high-peaked. The print leaves the first line’s rhyme word without a vowel (al-qalaq), gives al-ḥuraqi and munṭaliqi the rhyme’s -i where the grammar wants -u and -an, writes fī with a final ى in the last line, and has minki, “from you” (to a woman), in the third line but minka (to a man) in the fifth; all kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ إِنْشَادِهِ بَكَى وَبَكَى عَزِيزٌ مَعَهُ لِأَنَّهُ جَرِيحُ الْقَلْبِ
sentences.tr: thumma lammā faragha min inshādihi bakā wa-bakā ʿazīzun maʿahu li-annahu jarīḥu al-qalbi
sentences.l: Then when he finished from his reciting, he wept, and ʿAzīz wept with him, because he (was) wounded of the heart.
sentences.i: When he had finished reciting he wept, and ʿAzīz wept with him, for his own heart was wounded.

sentences.t: فَرَقَّ قَلْبُ الْوَزِيرِ لِبُكَائِهِمَا وَقَالَ يَاسَيِّدِي طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّعَيْنًا فَمَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا الْخَيْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-raqqa qalbu al-wazīri li-bukāʾihimā wa-qāla yā sayyidī ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan fa-mā yakūnu illā al-khayru
sentences.l: And the heart of the vizier softened for their weeping, and he said: O my lord, be-good of soul and be-cool of eye, for there will not be except the good.
sentences.i: The vizier’s heart was moved by their tears, and he said, “My lord, take heart and be of good cheer: nothing but good will come of it.”
sentences.n: ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan, “be good of soul and cool of eye”: the stock words of comfort; a cool eye is a contented one. li-, “for, because of”: li-bukāʾihimā, “at their weeping”. The print runs yā and sayyidī, and qarra and ʿaynan, together (ياسيدي, وقرّعينا); kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ يَاوَزِيرُ طَالَتْ مُدَّةُ السَّفَرِ فَأَخْبِرْنِي كَمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْبَلَدِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla tāju al-mulūki yā wazīru ṭālat muddatu al-safari fa-akhbirnī kam baynanā wa-bayna al-baladi
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said: O vizier, the length of the journey has grown-long; so inform me how-much (is) between us and between the city.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said, “Vizier, the journey has been long. Tell me how far we are from the city.”
sentences.n: kam baynanā wa-bayna, “how much between us and between”: Arabic repeats bayna with each term. The print runs yā and wazīru together (ياوزير); kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ عَزِيزٌ مَابَقِيَ إِلَّا الْقَلِيلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ʿazīzun mā baqiya illā al-qalīlu
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz said to him: There has not remained except the little.
sentences.i: ʿAzīz answered him, “Only a little way remains.”
sentences.n: The prince asks the vizier, but ʿAzīz, who knows the road, answers. The print runs mā and baqiya together (مابقي); kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَارُوا يَقْطَعُونَ الْأَوْدِيَةَ وَالْأَوْعَارَ وَالْبَرَارِيَ وَالْقِفَارَ
sentences.tr: thumma sārū yaqṭaʿūna al-awdiyata wa-al-awʿāra wa-al-barāriya wa-al-qifāra
sentences.l: Then they went-on cutting-across the valleys and the rugged-places and the wildernesses and the wastes.
sentences.i: Then they rode on, crossing valleys and rough country, wildernesses and wastes.
sentences.n: The prose rhymes on awʿār and qifār.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ نَائِمٌ إِذْرَأَى فِى النَّوْمِ أَنَّ مَحْبُوبَتَهُ مَعَهُ وَهُوَ يُعَانِقُهَا وَيَضُمُّهَا إِلَى صَدْرِهِ فَانْتَبَهَ مَرْعُوبًا فَزِعًا طَائِرَ الْعَقْلِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā tāju al-mulūki dhāta laylatin nāʾimun idh raʾā fī al-nawmi anna maḥbūbatahu maʿahu wa-huwa yuʿāniquhā wa-yaḍummuhā ilā ṣadrihi fa-intabaha marʿūban faziʿan ṭāʾira al-ʿaqli wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And while Tāj al-Mulūk, one night, (was) sleeping, behold, he saw in the sleep that his beloved (was) with him, and he embracing her and pressing her to his breast; and he woke terrified, frightened, flown of the mind, and recited, saying — verse:
sentences.i: One night, as Tāj al-Mulūk slept, he dreamed that his beloved was with him, and that he was embracing her and holding her to his breast. He woke in terror, startled out of his wits, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: baynamā … idh, “while … behold”: the pair that opens a sudden event. The print runs idh and raʾā together and writes raʾā without its hamza (اذراى); kept. ṭāʾir al-ʿaql, “flown of mind”, his wits scattered. shiʿr, “verse”, stands alone as a heading for the poem, as the print sometimes sets it.

sentences.t:
خَلِيلَيَّ هَامَ الْقَلْبُ وَالدَّمْعُ سَاجِمُ * وَوَجْدِي غَزِيْرٌ وَالْغَرَامُ مُلَازِمُ
وَنَوْحِي كَنَوْحِ الثَّاكِلَاتِ مِنَ الْبُكَا * اِذَا جَنَّ لَيْلِي نُحْتُ نَوْحَ الْحَمَائِمِ
وَاِنْ هَبَّتِ الْاَرْيَاحُ مِنْ نَحْوَارْضِكُمْ * وَجَدْتُ بِهَا بَرْدًا عَلَى الْاَرْضِ قَادِمِ
سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ كُلَّمَا هَبَّتِ الصَّبَا * وَمَا طَارَ قُمْرِيٌّ وَنَاحَتْ حَمَائِمُ
sentences.tr:
khalīlayya hāma al-qalbu wa-al-damʿu sājimu * wa-wajdī ghazīrun wa-al-gharāmu mulāzimu
wa-nawḥī ka-nawḥi al-thākilāti mina al-bukā * idhā janna laylī nuḥtu nawḥa al-ḥamāʾimi
wa-in habbati al-aryāḥu min naḥwa arḍikum * wajadtu bihā bardan ʿalā al-arḍi qādimi
salāmun ʿalaykum kullamā habbati al-ṣabā * wa-mā ṭāra qumriyyun wa-nāḥat ḥamāʾimu
sentences.l:
O my two friends, the heart has wandered-distraught, and the tear (is) pouring, * and my passion (is) abundant, and the love-torment (is) clinging.
And my lament (is) like the lament of the bereaved-women, from the weeping; * when my night grows-dark I lament the lament of the doves.
And if the winds blow from (the) direction of your land, * I find in them a coolness coming upon the earth.
Peace (be) upon you, whenever the east-wind blows, * and as-long-as a turtle-dove flies and doves lament.
sentences.i:
My two friends, my heart is distraught, my tears pour down, * my passion is deep, and love will not let me go.
I mourn like women mourning their dead, * and when my night grows dark I moan as the doves moan.
And if the winds blow from the quarter of your land, * I feel in them a coolness coming over the earth.
Peace be upon you, as often as the east wind blows, * as long as the turtle-dove flies and the doves lament.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed, except in the third line, where the print has al-arbāḥ (الْاَرْبَاحُ), “the profits”, a misprint for al-aryāḥ, “the winds”, corrected here. khalīlayya, “my two friends”, is the poet’s conventional address to two companions. The print runs naḥwa and arḍikum together (نَحْوَارْضِكُمْ); kept. qādimi, “coming”, takes the rhyme’s -i where the grammar wants qādiman. al-ṣabā is the east wind, the lover’s messenger in Arabic verse; a qumrī is a turtle-dove.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ مِنْ إِنْشَادِهِ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَبْشِرْ هَذِهِ عَلَامَةُ الْخَيْرِ فَطِبْ قَلْبًا وَقَرَّعَيْنًا وَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ تَبْلُغَ مَقْصُودَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha tāju al-mulūki min inshādihi aqbala ʿalayhi al-wazīru wa-qāla lahu abshir hādhihi ʿalāmatu al-khayri fa-ṭib qalban wa-qarra ʿaynan wa-lā budda an tablugha maqṣūdaka
sentences.l: And when Tāj al-Mulūk finished from his reciting, the vizier came-towards him and said to him: Rejoice! This (is) the sign of the good; so be-good of heart and cool of eye, and (there is) no escape that you reach your aim.
sentences.i: When Tāj al-Mulūk had finished, the vizier came to him and said, “Good news! This is a sign of good fortune. Take heart and be of good cheer: you will surely reach your goal.”
sentences.n: The vizier reads the dream as an omen. lā budda an, “there is no escape from (it) that”, i.e. “surely”. The print again runs qarra and ʿaynan together (وقرّعينا); kept.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَزِيزٌ وَصَبَّرَهُ وَصَارَ يُلْهِيهِ وَيُحَادِثُهُ وَيَحْكِي لَهُ الْحِكَايَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala ʿalayhi ʿazīzun wa-ṣabbarahu wa-ṣāra yulhīhi wa-yuḥādithuhu wa-yaḥkī lahu al-ḥikāyāti
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz came-towards him and made-him-patient, and began to divert him and converse with him and tell him the tales.
sentences.i: ʿAzīz came to him too and consoled him, and kept him amused with talk and stories.

sentences.t: وَهُمْ يَجِدُّونَ فِى السَّيْرِ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا مُسَافِرِينَ أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ إِلَى مُدَّةِ شَهْرَيْنِ آخَرَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-hum yajiddūna fī al-sayri wa-lam yazālū musāfirīna ayyāman wa-layāliya ilā muddati shahrayni ākharayni
sentences.l: And they (were) hastening in the going, and they did not cease travelling days and nights, up to a space of two months other.
sentences.i: They pressed on with their journey, travelling days and nights, for two months more.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ أَشْرَقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّمْسُ وَلَاحَ لَهُمْ مِنَ الْبُعْدِ شَيْءٌ أَبْيَضُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna yawman mina al-ayyāmi ashraqat ʿalayhimu al-shamsu wa-lāḥa lahum mina al-buʿdi shayʾun abyaḍu
sentences.l: And when it was a day of the days, the sun rose upon them, and there appeared to them from the distance a thing white.
sentences.i: Then one day, as the sun rose upon them, something white came into view in the distance.
sentences.n: kāna yawman, “it was one day”: kāna with its subject unexpressed (“it, the time”) and yawman as its predicate; a set phrase of the tale.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ لِعَزِيزٍ مَاهَذَا الْبَيَاضُ فَقَالَ عَزِيزٌ يَامَوْلَايَ هَذِهِ الْقَلْعَةُ الْبَيْضَاءُ وَهَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةُ الَّتِي أَنْتَ طَالِبُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla tāju al-mulūki li-ʿazīzin mā hādhā al-bayāḍu fa-qāla ʿazīzun yā mawlāya hādhihi al-qalʿatu al-bayḍāʾu wa-hādhihi al-madīnatu allatī anta ṭālibuhā
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz: What (is) this whiteness? And ʿAzīz said: O my master, this (is) the White Castle, and this (is) the city which you (are) seeking.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz, “What is that whiteness?” ʿAzīz said, “My lord, that is the White Castle, and that is the city you are seeking.”
sentences.n: The print runs mā and hādhā, and yā and mawlāya, together (ماهذا, يامولاي); kept. ʿAzīz knows the city: he came here once as a merchant and glimpsed the lady Dunyā in her garden, and he has just been here again with the embassy.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا مُسَافِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبُوا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ فَلَمَّا قَرُبُوا مِنْهَا فَرِحَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ وَزَالَ عَنْهُ الْهَمُّ وَالتَّرَحُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa tāju al-mulūki wa-lam yazālū musāfirīna ilā an qarubū mina al-madīnati fa-lammā qarubū minhā fariḥa tāju al-mulūki ghāyata al-faraḥi wa-zāla ʿanhu al-hammu wa-al-taraḥu
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk rejoiced, and they did not cease travelling until they came-near to the city; and when they came-near to it, Tāj al-Mulūk rejoiced the utmost of the joy, and the care and the sorrow left him.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk was glad, and they travelled on until they drew near the city; and as they drew near it he rejoiced beyond measure, and his care and sorrow left him.
sentences.n: faraḥ and taraḥ, “joy” and “sorrow”, are a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلُوهَا وَهُمْ فِي سِيمَةِ التُّجَّارِ وَابْنُ الْمَلِكِ فِي زِيِّ تَاجِرٍ كَبِيرٍ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhalūhā wa-hum fī sīmati al-tujjāri wa-ibnu al-maliki fī ziyyi tājirin kabīrin
sentences.l: Then they entered it, and they (were) in the mark of the merchants, and the son of the king in the dress of a great merchant.
sentences.i: Then they entered it in the guise of merchants, the king’s son dressed as a great merchant.
sentences.n: sīma, “mark, appearance”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَتَوْا إِلَى مَكَانٍ يُعْرَفُ بِمَنْزِلِ التُّجَّارِ وَهُوَ خَانٌ عَظِيمٌ
sentences.tr: thumma ataw ilā makānin yuʿrafu bi-manzili al-tujjāri wa-huwa khānun ʿaẓīmun
sentences.l: Then they came to a place (that) is known by (the name) the Lodging of the Merchants, and it (is) a great khan.
sentences.i: Then they came to a place called the Merchants’ Lodging, a great inn.
sentences.n: ʿurifa bi-, “to be known by (the name of)”. A khān is a caravanserai, an inn for merchants and their goods.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ لِعَزِيزٍ أَهَذَا مَحَلُّ التُّجَّارِ فَقَالَ عَزِيزٌ نَعَمْ وَهُوَ الْخَانُ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أَنَا نَزَلْتُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla tāju al-mulūki li-ʿazīzin a-hādhā maḥallu al-tujjāri fa-qāla ʿazīzun naʿam wa-huwa al-khānu alladhī kuntu anā nazaltu fīhi
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz: Is this the place of the merchants? And ʿAzīz said: Yes, and it (is) the khan which I had, I, lodged in.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk said to ʿAzīz, “Is this the merchants’ place?” ʿAzīz said, “Yes, and it is the very inn where I stayed before.”
sentences.n: a-hādhā, “is this?”: a- marks a question. kuntu … nazaltu, “I had lodged”: kāna with a perfect gives the pluperfect.

sentences.t: فَأَنْزَلُوا فِيهِ وَأَنَاخُوا فِيهِ مَطِيَّهُمْ وَحَطُّوا رِحَالَهُمْ وَخَزَنُوا أَمْتِعَتَهُمْ فِى الْمَخَازِنِ وَأَقَامُوا لِلرَّاحَةِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-anzalū fīhi wa-anākhū fīhi maṭiyyahum wa-ḥaṭṭū riḥālahum wa-khazanū amtiʿatahum fī al-makhāzini wa-aqāmū li-al-rāḥati arbaʿata ayyāmin
sentences.l: And they set-down (their company) in it, and made their mounts kneel in it, and put down their saddle-bags, and stored their goods in the storerooms, and stayed for the rest four days.
sentences.i: So they put up there, couched their camels, unloaded their baggage and stored their goods in the storerooms, and rested there four days.
sentences.n: fa-anzalū, “they set down (their company)”: the print has the causative, where the plain fa-nazalū, “they alighted”, is what the sense wants; it may be a slip, and is kept as printed. anākha, “to make (a camel) kneel”. maṭiyy, “mounts”, a collective. li-al-rāḥa, “for rest”: li- gives the purpose.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَشَارَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْ يَكْتَرُوا لَهُمْ دَارًا كَبِيرَةً فَأَجَابُوهُ وَاكْتَرَوْا لَهُمْ دَارًا وَاسِعَةَ الْبُنْيَانِ مُعَدَّةً لِلْأَفْرَاحِ فَنَزَلُوا فِيهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra ashāra ʿalayhim an yaktarū lahum dāran kabīratan fa-ajābūhu wa-iktaraw lahum dāran wāsiʿata al-bunyāni muʿaddatan li-al-afrāḥi fa-nazalū fīhā
sentences.l: Then (truly) the vizier advised them that they hire for themselves a big house; and they answered him, and hired for themselves a house wide of building, prepared for the festivities, and they lodged in it.
sentences.i: Then the vizier advised them to rent a large house. They agreed, and rented a spacious house fit for celebrations, and moved into it.
sentences.n: ashāra ʿalā, “to advise”. iktarā, “to hire, rent”; lahum, “for them”, here “for themselves”. muʿadda li-al-afrāḥ, “made ready for festivities”: li- gives the purpose; a house fit for weddings and feasts.

sentences.t: وَأَقَامَ الْوَزِيرُ وَعَزِيزٌ يُدَبِّرَانِ حِيلَةً لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَتَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ حَائِرٌ لَا يَدْرِي مَايَفْعَلُ وَلَمْ يَجِدْ لَهُ حِيلَةً غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ تَاجَرَ فِي قَيْصَرِيَّةِ الْبَزِّ
sentences.tr: wa-aqāma al-wazīru wa-ʿazīzun yudabbirāni ḥīlatan li-tāji al-mulūki wa-tāju al-mulūki ḥāʾirun lā yadrī mā yafʿalu wa-lam yajid lahu ḥīlatan ghayra annahu tājara fī qayṣariyyati al-bazzi
sentences.l: And the vizier and ʿAzīz stayed devising a stratagem for Tāj al-Mulūk, and Tāj al-Mulūk (was) bewildered, not knowing what he should do, and he did not find for himself a stratagem other than that he traded in the qayṣariyya of the cloth.
sentences.i: The vizier and ʿAzīz set about devising a plan for Tāj al-Mulūk, while he was at a loss, not knowing what to do, and could find no scheme except to trade in the cloth market.
sentences.n: A qayṣariyya is a covered market of shops, usually for costly goods; bazz is cloth, especially linen and fine stuffs. tājara, “he traded”, is read here as the verb; the same letters could be tājir, “a merchant” (“other than that he was a merchant”). The verb aqāma is singular before its two subjects, as Arabic allows. The print runs mā and yafʿalu together (مايفعل); kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَعَزِيزٍ وَقَالَ لَهُمَا اعْلَمَا أَنَّهُ إِذَا كَانَ مُقَامُنَا هُنَا عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ فَإِنَّنَا لَا نَبْلُغُ مُرَادَنَا وَلَا تُقْضَي لَنَا حَاجَةٌ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra aqbala ʿalā tāji al-mulūki wa-ʿazīzin wa-qāla lahumā iʿlamā annahu idhā kāna muqāmunā hunā ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati fa-innanā lā nablughu murādanā wa-lā tuqḍā lanā ḥājatun
sentences.l: Then (truly) the vizier came-towards Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz and said to the two: Know (you two) that, if our staying here is upon this state, then we do not reach our desire, and no need is fulfilled for us.
sentences.i: Then the vizier came to Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz and said to them, “Understand this: if we go on staying here as we are, we will never get what we want, and nothing we need will be done.
sentences.n: iʿlamā, “know (you two)”, the dual imperative. The print writes tuqḍā, “is fulfilled”, with a final ي (تقضي); kept.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَطَرَ بِبَالِي شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ الصَّلَاحُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad khaṭara bi-bālī shayʾun wa-huwa in shāʾa allāhu fīhi al-ṣalāḥu
sentences.l: And there has occurred in my mind a thing, and it, if God wills, in it (is) the good.
sentences.i: But something has come into my mind, and in it, God willing, lies the answer.”
sentences.n: khaṭara bi-bālihi, “it occurred to him”: bi- here means “in”, the mind being where the thought comes.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَعَزِيزٌ افْعَلْ مَابَدَا لَكَ فَإِنَّ الْمَشَائِخَ فِيهِمُ الْبَرَكَةُ لَا سِيَّمَا أَنَّكَ قَدْ مَارَسْتَ الْأُمُورَ فَقُلْ لَنَا مَاخَطَرَ بِبَالِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu tāju al-mulūki wa-ʿazīzun ifʿal mā badā laka fa-inna al-mashāʾikha fīhimu al-barakatu lā siyyamā annaka qad mārasta al-umūra fa-qul lanā mā khaṭara bi-bālika
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz said to him: Do what has appeared (good) to you, for the elders, in them (is) the blessing; especially that you have practised the affairs. So say to us what has occurred in your mind.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz said to him, “Do whatever you think best: there is blessing in the old, all the more since you are practised in affairs. So tell us what has come into your mind.”
sentences.n: al-mashāʾikh, “the elders” (sing. shaykh), with a hamza where Classical has mashāyikh, a common form. lā siyyamā, “especially”. The print runs mā badā and mā khaṭara together (مابدا, ماخطر); kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ الرَّأْيُ أَنَّنَا نَكْتَرِي لَكَ دُكَّانًا فِي سُوقِ الْبَزِّ تَقْعُدُ فِيهَا لِلْبَيْعِ وَالشِّرَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-tāji al-mulūki al-raʾyu annanā naktarī laka dukkānan fī sūqi al-bazzi taqʿudu fīhā li-al-bayʿi wa-al-shirāʾi
sentences.l: And he said to Tāj al-Mulūk: The opinion (is) that we hire for you a shop in the market of the cloth, (that) you sit in it for the selling and the buying,
sentences.i: He said to Tāj al-Mulūk, “My advice is that we rent you a shop in the cloth market, where you can sit and buy and sell;
sentences.n: dukkān, “shop”, is treated as feminine here (fīhā), as often in this text.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ كُلَّوَاحِدٍ مِنَ الْخَاصِّ وَالْعَامِّ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْبَزِّ وَالتَّفَاصِيلِ
sentences.tr: li-anna kulla wāḥidin mina al-khāṣṣi wa-al-ʿāmmi yaḥtāju ilā al-bazzi wa-al-tafāṣīli
sentences.l: because every one of the elite and the common needs (to) the cloth and the cut-lengths;
sentences.i: for everyone, high and low, needs cloth and dress-lengths.
sentences.n: The print runs kulla and wāḥidin together (كلواحد); kept. al-khāṣṣ wa-al-ʿāmm, “the special and the common”, high and low. tafāṣīl, “pieces cut to length”, lengths of cloth for garments.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا سَكَنْتَ وَقَعَدْتَ فِي تِلْكَ الدُّكَّانِ يَنْصَلِحُ أَمْرُكَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى خُصُوصًا وَصُورَتُكَ جَمِيلَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā sakanta wa-qaʿadta fī tilka al-dukkāni yanṣaliḥu amruka in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā khuṣūṣan wa-ṣūratuka jamīlatun
sentences.l: And if you settle and sit in that shop, your affair will come-right, if God, (He is) exalted, wills, especially and your form (is) beautiful.
sentences.i: Once you are settled in that shop, your affair will come right, God willing, all the more because you are so handsome.
sentences.n: yanṣaliḥu, “comes right”, a form VII of ṣalaḥa found in the spoken language. khuṣūṣan wa-, “especially since”.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنِ اجْعَلْ عَزِيزًا أَمِينًا عِنْدَكَ وَأَجْلِسْهُ فِي دَاخِلِ الدُّكَّانِ لِيُنَا وِلَكَ التَّفَاصِيلَ وَالْأَقْمِشَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākini ijʿal ʿazīzan amīnan ʿindaka wa-ajlishu fī dākhili al-dukkāni li-yunāwilaka al-tafāṣīla wa-al-aqmishata
sentences.l: But make ʿAzīz a trusted-one with you, and seat him in the inside of the shop, so that he hands you the cut-lengths and the fabrics.
sentences.i: But make ʿAzīz your trusted man, and seat him at the back of the shop to hand you the lengths and fabrics.”
sentences.n: The print breaks li-yunāwilaka, “so that he may hand you”, into two words (لينا ولك); the spacing is kept, and the word is read whole. amīn, “trustworthy”, here a shop’s confidential clerk.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ قَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا رَأْيٌ سَدِيدٌ وَمَلِيحٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa tāju al-mulūki dhālika al-kalāma qāla inna hādhā raʾyun sadīdun wa-malīḥun
sentences.l: And when Tāj al-Mulūk heard that speech, he said: Truly this (is) an opinion sound and fine.
sentences.i: When Tāj al-Mulūk heard this he said, “This is sound advice, and good.”

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَخْرَجَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ بَدْلَةً سَنِيَّةً تُجَّارِيَّةً وَلَبِسَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika akhraja tāju al-mulūki badlatan saniyyatan tujjāriyyatan wa-labisahā
sentences.l: And at that Tāj al-Mulūk brought out a suit splendid, merchant-like, and put it on.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk brought out a splendid merchant’s suit of clothes and put it on.
sentences.n: The print has تجّاربة, a misprint for تجّارية, corrected here: tujjāriyya, “of the merchants’ kind”. badla, “a suit of clothes”.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ يَمْشِي وَغِلْمَانُهُ خَلْفَهُ وَأَعْطَي لِأَحَدِهِمْ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ مَعَهُ لِيَقْضِيَ بِهَا مَصَالِحَ الدُّكَّانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma yamshī wa-ghilmānuhu khalfahu wa-aʿṭā li-aḥadihim alfa dīnārin maʿahu li-yaqḍiya bihā maṣāliḥa al-dukkāni
sentences.l: And he rose walking, and his servants behind him, and he gave to one of them a thousand dinars (to keep) with him, so that he might settle with it the needs of the shop.
sentences.i: He set out on foot with his servants behind him, and gave one of them a thousand dinars to carry, to pay for what the shop would need.
sentences.n: aʿṭā li-, “to give to”: spoken Arabic marks the receiver with li-, where Classical has a second object. The print writes aʿṭā with a final ي (اعطي); kept. bihā, “with it”: the money. maṣāliḥ, “requirements, business”.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالُوا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى سُوقِ الْبَزِّ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna ilā an waṣalū ilā sūqi al-bazzi
sentences.l: And they did not cease going until they arrived at the market of the cloth.
sentences.i: They walked on until they came to the cloth market.
sentences.n: The print has سرق, a misprint for سوق, corrected here.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ التُّجَّارُ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ وَنَظَرُوا إِلَى حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ تَحَيَّرُوا وَصَارُوا يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ رِضْوَانَ فَتَحَ أَبْوَابَ الْجِنَانِ وَغَفَلَ عَنْهَا فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا هَذَا الشَّابُّ الْبَدِيعُ الْحُسْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾati al-tujjāru tāja al-mulūki wa-naẓarū ilā ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi taḥayyarū wa-ṣārū yaqūlūna inna riḍwāna fataḥa abwāba al-jināni wa-ghafala ʿanhā fa-kharaja minhā hādhā al-shābbu al-badīʿu al-ḥusni
sentences.l: And when the merchants saw Tāj al-Mulūk and looked at his beauty and his loveliness, they were bewildered, and began saying: Truly Riḍwān opened the gates of the Gardens and was-heedless of them, so there came out from them this youth, the wondrous of beauty.
sentences.i: When the merchants saw Tāj al-Mulūk and beheld his beauty and grace, they were amazed and began to say, “Riḍwān must have opened the gates of Paradise and looked away, and this marvellously handsome youth slipped out.”
sentences.n: raʾati al-tujjāru, “the merchants saw”: the verb is feminine before a broken plural, as Arabic allows. Riḍwān is the angel who keeps the gates of Paradise; al-jinān, “the Gardens”, is Paradise.

sentences.t: وَآخَرُ يَقُولُ لَعَلَّ هَذَا مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ākharu yaqūlu laʿalla hādhā mina al-malāʾikati
sentences.l: And another saying: Perhaps this (is) of the angels.
sentences.i: And another would say, “Perhaps he is one of the angels.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عِنْدَ التُّجَّارِ سَأَلُوا عَنْ دُكَّانِ الْعَرِيفِ فَدَلُّوهُمْ عَلَيْهَا فَمَازَالُوا سَائِرِينَ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا عِنْدَ الْعَرِيفِ فَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalū ʿinda al-tujjāri saʾalū ʿan dukkāni al-ʿarīfi fa-dallūhum ʿalayhā fa-mā zālū sāʾirīna ḥattā waṣalū ʿinda al-ʿarīfi fa-sallamū ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And when they went-in among the merchants, they asked about the shop of the ʿarīf, and they guided them to it; and they did not cease going until they arrived at the ʿarīf, and greeted him.
sentences.i: When they had come in among the merchants, they asked for the shop of the headman of the market, and were shown the way to it. They walked on until they reached him, and greeted him.
sentences.n: al-ʿarīf, “the one who knows”, is the headman of a trade or market, who answers for its members; the print gives the word a vowel (العَريف) here and several times after. waṣala ʿinda, “to arrive at”, with ʿinda for Classical ilā, as in speech. The print runs mā zālū together (فمازالوا); kept.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِمْ هُوَ وَمَنْ عِنْدَةُ مِنَ التُّجَّارِ وَأَجْلَسُوهُمْ وَعَظَّمُوهُمْ لِأَجْلِ الْوَزِيرِ فَإِنَّهُمْ رَأَوْهُ رَجُلًا كَبِيرًا مَهَابًا وَمَعَهُ الشَّابُّ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَعَزِيزٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma ilayhim huwa wa-man ʿindahu mina al-tujjāri wa-ajlasūhum wa-ʿaẓẓamūhum li-ajli al-wazīri fa-innahum raʾawhu rajulan kabīran mahāban wa-maʿahu al-shābbu tāju al-mulūki wa-ʿazīzun
sentences.l: And he rose to them, he and whoever (was) with him of the merchants, and they seated them and honoured them for the sake of the vizier, for they saw him a man old, awe-inspiring, and with him the youth Tāj al-Mulūk, and ʿAzīz.
sentences.i: He rose to meet them, he and the merchants who were with him, and they seated them and showed them great honour for the vizier’s sake, for they saw that he was an aged and imposing man, with the young Tāj al-Mulūk and ʿAzīz beside him.
sentences.n: qāma ilā, “to rise (to greet)”. The print spells ʿindahu, “with him”, with a final ة (عندة), as it does now and then; kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ التُّجَّارُ لِبَعْضِهِمْ لَا شَكَّ أَنَّ هَذَا الشَّيْخَ وَالِدُ هَذَيْنِ الشَّابَّيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-tujjāru li-baʿḍihim lā shakka anna hādhā al-shaykha wālidu hādhayni al-shābbayni
sentences.l: And the merchants said to (the) some of them: No doubt that this old-man (is) the father of these two youths.
sentences.i: The merchants said to one another, “No doubt this old man is the father of these two young men.”
sentences.n: li-baʿḍihim, “to some of them”, i.e. to one another.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْوَزِيرُ مَنْ شَيْخُ السُّوقِ فِيكُمْ فَقَالُوا هَاهُوَ وَإِذَا هُوَ أَقْبَلَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-wazīru man shaykhu al-sūqi fīkum fa-qālū hā huwa wa-idhā huwa aqbala
sentences.l: And the vizier said to them: Who (is) the elder of the market among you? And they said: Here he (is)! And behold, he came-forward.
sentences.i: The vizier said to them, “Which of you is the headman of the market?” They said, “There he is,” and at that moment he came up.
sentences.n: hā huwa, “here he is”, is printed as one word (هاهو); kept. wa-idhā, “and behold”, marks the sudden appearance.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَتَأَمَّلَهُ فَرَآهُ شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا صَاحِبَ هَيْبَةٍ وَوَقَارٍ وَخَدَمٍ وَغِلْمَانٍ وَعَبِيدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilayhi al-wazīru wa-taʾammalahu fa-raʾāhu shaykhan kabīran ṣāḥiba haybatin wa-waqārin wa-khadamin wa-ghilmānin wa-ʿabīdin
sentences.l: And the vizier looked at him and considered him, and saw him an old-man, aged, possessor of awe and gravity, and servants and pages and slaves.
sentences.i: The vizier looked at him closely and saw an aged man of great dignity and presence, with servants, pages and slaves.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ حَيَّاهُمُ الْعَرِيفُ تَحِيَّةَ الْأَحْبَابِ وَبَالَغَ فِي إِكْرَامِهِمْ وَأَجْلَسَهُمْ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ḥayyāhumu al-ʿarīfu taḥiyyata al-aḥbābi wa-bālagha fī ikrāmihim wa-ajlasahum ilā jānibihi
sentences.l: And at that the ʿarīf greeted them (with) the greeting of the beloved-ones, and went-to-lengths in honouring them, and seated them at his side.
sentences.i: Then the headman greeted them as one greets dear friends, did them every honour and seated them beside him.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُمْ هَلْ لَكُمْ مِنْ حَاجَةٍ نَفُوزُ بِقَضَائُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahum hal lakum min ḥājatin nafūzu bi-qaḍāʾuhā
sentences.l: And he said to them: Is there to you any need (that) we may win (with) the fulfilling of it?
sentences.i: And he said to them, “Have you any need that we might have the honour of meeting?”
sentences.n: fāza bi-, “to win, gain”: bi- names the prize; to meet their need would be his good fortune. min ḥājatin, “any need”: min after a question means “any at all”. The print points the hamza with a ḍamma (بقضائُها) where the case after bi- wants a kasra; the print’s mark is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ نَعَمْ أَنَا رَجُلٌ كَبِيرٌ طَاعِنٌ فِى السِّنِّ وَمَعِي هَذَانِ الْغُلَامَانِ وَسَافَرْتُ بِهِمَا سَائِرَ الْأَقَالِيمِ وَالْبِلَادِ وَمَا دَخَلْتُ بَلْدَةً إِلَّا أَقَمْتُ بِهَا سَنَةً كَامِلَةً حَتَّى يَتَفَرَّجَا عَلَيْهَا وَيَعْرِفَا أَهْلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru naʿam anā rajulun kabīrun ṭāʿinun fī al-sinni wa-maʿī hādhāni al-ghulāmāni wa-sāfartu bihimā sāʾira al-aqālīmi wa-al-bilādi wa-mā dakhaltu baldatan illā aqamtu bihā sanatan kāmilatan ḥattā yatafarrajā ʿalayhā wa-yaʿrifā ahlahā
sentences.l: And the vizier said: Yes. I (am) a man old, advanced in the age, and with me (are) these two lads; and I have travelled with them (through) all the regions and the lands, and I did not enter a town but I stayed in it a year complete, so that the two might look-around at it and know its people.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Yes. I am an old man, far on in years, and these two young men are with me. I have travelled with them through every region and country, and never entered a town without staying a full year, so that they could see its sights and come to know its people.
sentences.n: The print has ينفرّجا, a misprint for يتفرّجا, corrected here. tafarraja ʿalā, “to look about at, enjoy the sights of”. sāfara bi-, “to travel with”: bi- takes the companions along. ghulām, “lad, young man”: the vizier calls the two his boys. ṭāʿin fī al-sinn, “advanced in years”, literally “piercing into age”.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي قَدْ أَتَيْتُ بِلَادَكُمْ هَذِةِ وَاخْتَرْتُ الْمُقَامَ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-innī qad ataytu bilādakum hādhihi wa-ikhtartu al-muqāma fīhā
sentences.l: And (truly) I have come (to) this land of yours, and chosen the staying in it,
sentences.i: Now I have come to your country and chosen to stay here,
sentences.n: The print has بالدنكم, a misprint for بلادكم, corrected here: the alif and the lām have changed places and a stray tooth has crept in; the feminine hādhihi that follows fits bilād, “country”. The print spells hādhihi with a final ة (هذة), as it does three times in this night; kept.

sentences.t: وَأَشْتَهِي مِنْكَ دُكَّانًا تَكُونُ جَيِّدَةً مِنْ أَحْسَنِ الْمَوَاضِعِ حَتَّى أُجْلِسَهُمَا فِيهَا لِيَتَّجِرَا وَيَتَفَرَّجَا عَلَى هَذِةِ الْبَلْدَةِ وَيَتَخَلَّقَا بِأَخْلَاقِ أَهْلِهَا وَيَتَعَلَّمَا الْبَيْعَ وَالشِّرَاءَ وَالْأَخْذَ وَالْعَطَاءَ
sentences.tr: wa-ashtahī minka dukkānan takūnu jayyidatan min aḥsani al-mawāḍiʿi ḥattā ujlisahumā fīhā li-yattajirā wa-yatafarrajā ʿalā hādhihi al-baldati wa-yatakhallaqā bi-akhlāqi ahlihā wa-yataʿallamā al-bayʿa wa-al-shirāʾa wa-al-akhdha wa-al-ʿaṭāʾa
sentences.l: and I desire from you a shop (that) will be good, of the best of the places, so that I may seat the two in it, that they may trade and look-around at this town, and take-on the manners of its people, and learn the selling and the buying, the taking and the giving.
sentences.i: and I would like you to find me a good shop in one of the best places, so that I can set them up in it to trade and see the sights of this town, take on the ways of its people, and learn to buy and sell, to take and give.”
sentences.n: ishtahā min, “to desire from”, a polite request. takhallaqa bi-, “to take on (manners)”: bi- names the character adopted. al-akhdh wa-al-ʿaṭāʾ, “taking and giving”, the give-and-take of trade.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعَرِيفُ لَابَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿarīfu lā baʾsa bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And the ʿarīf said: No harm in that.
sentences.i: The headman said, “By all means.”
sentences.n: lā baʾsa bi-, “there is no harm in”: a set phrase of consent, printed run together and without its hamza (لاباس); kept.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الْعَرِيفُ إِلَى الْوَلَدَيْنِ وَفَرِحَ بِهِمَا وَأَحَبَّهُمَا حُبًّا زَائِدًا
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-ʿarīfu ilā al-waladayni wa-fariḥa bihimā wa-aḥabbahumā ḥubban zāʾidan
sentences.l: And the ʿarīf looked at the two boys, and rejoiced in them, and loved them a love exceeding.
sentences.i: The headman looked at the two young men and was delighted with them, and loved them beyond measure.
sentences.n: The print has زئدا, a misprint for زائدا, corrected here. fariḥa bi-, “to be delighted with”: bi- names the cause of the joy.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْعَرِيفُ مُغْرَمًا بِفَاتِكِ اللَّحَظَاتِ وَيُغَلِّبُ حُبَّ الْبَنِينَ عَلَى الْبَنَاتِ وَيَمِيلُ إِلَى الْحُمُوضَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-ʿarīfu mughraman bi-fātiki al-laḥaẓāti wa-yughallibu ḥubba al-banīna ʿalā al-banāti wa-yamīlu ilā al-ḥumūḍati
sentences.l: And the ʿarīf was enamoured of (the one) murderous of the glances, and he would-give-the-upper-hand (to) the love of the boys over the girls, and he inclined to the sourness.
sentences.i: For the headman was a slave to deadly glances: he set the love of boys above the love of girls, and had a taste for sourness.
sentences.n: The print has ابنات, a misprint for البنات, corrected here. mughram bi-, “infatuated with”: bi- names the object of desire. fātik al-laḥaẓāt, “murderous of glances”, is the stock phrase for a beautiful youth whose eyes slay. ghallaba … ʿalā, “to prefer … over”. al-ḥumūḍa, “sourness”, seems to be slang for the same taste; the exact sense is not certain. The two he has his eye on are the young men before him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ هَذِةِ صَيْدَةٌ مَلِيحَةٌ سُبْحَانَ خَالِقِهِمَا وَمُصَوِّرِهِمَا مِنْ مَاءٍ مَهِينٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi hādhihi ṣaydatun malīḥatun subḥāna khāliqihimā wa-muṣawwirihimā min māʾin mahīnin
sentences.l: And he said in himself: This (is) a quarry fine! Glory (to) their Creator and their Fashioner from a water despised!
sentences.i: He said to himself, “Here is fine game! Glory be to Him who created them and fashioned them from a lowly fluid!”
sentences.n: ṣayda, “a catch, a quarry”, as in hunting. min māʾin mahīn, “from a despised water”, echoes the Qurʾān (77:20), where it names the fluid from which man is made.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَقَفَ الْعَرِيفُ لِخِدْمَتِهِمَا كَالْغُلَامِ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika waqafa al-ʿarīfu li-khidmatihimā ka-al-ghulāmi bayna aydīhimā
sentences.l: And at that the ʿarīf stood for their service like the servant-boy between their hands.
sentences.i: At that the headman stood ready to serve them like a page before them.
sentences.n: li-, “for”: li-khidmatihimā, “to serve them”. ka-, “like”. bayna aydīhimā, “between their hands”, i.e. in their presence.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَامَ وَهَيَّأَ لَهُمَا الدُّكَّانَ وَكَانَتْ فِي وَسَطِ الْقَيْصَرِيَّةِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ أَكْبَرُ وَلَا أَوْجَهُ مِنْهَا فِى السُّوقِ عِنْدَهُمْ لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ مُتَّسِعَةً مُزَخْرَفَةً فِيهَا رُفُوفٌ مِنْ عَاجٍ وَخَشَبِ الْآبَنُوسِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qāma wa-hayyaʾa lahumā al-dukkāna wa-kānat fī wasaṭi al-qayṣariyyati wa-lam yakun akbaru wa-lā awjahu minhā fī al-sūqi ʿindahum li-annahā kānat muttasiʿatan muzakhrafatan fīhā rufūfun min ʿājin wa-khashabi al-ābanūsi
sentences.l: Then (truly) he rose and prepared for the two the shop; and it was in the middle of the qayṣariyya, and there was not (one) bigger nor more-prominent than it in the market among them, because it was spacious, ornamented, in it shelves of ivory and wood of the ebony.
sentences.i: Then he rose and made the shop ready for them. It stood in the middle of the covered market, and there was none in their market larger or finer, for it was spacious and richly decorated, with shelves of ivory and ebony.
sentences.n: lam yakun akbaru, “there was not (one) larger”: kāna here means “there was”. awjah, “more prominent”, from wajh, “face”: a shop with the best frontage. The print spells ābanūs, “ebony”, with a madda (الآبنوس).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ الْمَفَاتِيحَ لِلْوَزِيرِ وَهُوَ فِي صِفَةِ الشَّيْخِ التَّاجِرِ وَقَالَ لَهُ خُذْ يَاسَيِّدِي جَعَلَهَا اللَّهُ مَنْزِلًا مُبَارَكًا عَلَى وَلَدَيْكَ
sentences.tr: thumma sallama al-mafātīḥa li-al-wazīri wa-huwa fī ṣifati al-shaykhi al-tājiri wa-qāla lahu khudh yā sayyidī jaʿalahā allāhu manzilan mubārakan ʿalā waladayka
sentences.l: Then he handed-over the keys to the vizier, and he (was) in the guise of the old-man the merchant, and said to him: Take, O my lord; (may) God make it a dwelling blessed upon your two sons.
sentences.i: Then he handed the keys to the vizier, who was playing the part of the old merchant, and said to him, “Take them, my lord, and may God make it a blessed place for your sons.”
sentences.n: sallama li-, “to hand over to”: li- marks the receiver. jaʿalahā allāh, “may God make it”: the perfect as a wish. The print runs yā and sayyidī together (ياسيدي); kept.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ مِنْهُ الْمَفَاتِيحَ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ مَضَوْا إِلَى الْخَانِ الَّذِي وَضَعُوا فِيهِ أَمْتِعَتَهُمْ وَأَمَرُوا الْغِلْمَانَ أَنْ يَنْقُلُوا جَمِيعَ مَا مَعَهُمْ مِنَ الْبَضَائِعِ وَالْقُمَاشِ إِلَى تِلْكَ الدُّكَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha minhu al-mafātīḥa thumma innahum maḍaw ilā al-khāni alladhī waḍaʿū fīhi amtiʿatahum wa-amarū al-ghilmāna an yanqulū jamīʿa mā maʿahum mina al-baḍāʾiʿi wa-al-qumāshi ilā tilka al-dukkāni
sentences.l: And he took from him the keys; then (truly) they went to the khan in which they had put their goods, and they ordered the servants that they carry all of what (was) with them of the wares and the cloth to that shop.
sentences.i: He took the keys from him. Then they went to the inn where they had left their goods, and ordered the servants to carry everything they had, wares and cloth, to the shop.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
